headline: Ex-MP Akhtaruzzaman denied bail in airport assault case
summary: A Dhaka court has rejected the bail plea of former lawmaker Major (retd) Akhtaruzzaman for allegedly assaulting a security official at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.
details: A Dhaka court has rejected the bail petition of former lawmaker Major (retd) Akhtaruzzaman in a case filed over assaulting an on-duty security official and obstructing government work at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.

The incident occurred on October 1 near the baggage belt area after passengers arriving from Madina on a Biman flight faced luggage delays and a shortage of trolleys, leading to agitation among passengers.
According to the complaint, Akhtaruzzaman allegedly hurled abuse at Airport Executive Director Group Captain SM Ragib Samad and threatened to 'grab him by the neck and throw him out.'

The situation escalated when security supervisor Warrant Officer Mohammad Kamal Uddin asked people accompanying the lawmaker to stop filming in a restricted area. Akhtaruzzaman allegedly verbally abused and physically assaulted him.
The case statement further alleges that the lawmaker threw bottles of Zamzam water off trolleys, damaging them, and behaved rudely toward a Biman representative.
Akhtaruzzaman was arrested from his residence in the Dhaka Cantonment area on October 2 and was placed on a one-day remand before being sent to jail.
The former lawmaker, who joined Jamaat-e-Islami in December last year after being expelled from the BNP, remains in custody.
caption:
An ex-MP allegedly assaulted a security official and threw Zamzam water bottles at the airport. Now, a court has denied him bail.

A Dhaka court has rejected the bail petition of former lawmaker Major (retd) Akhtaruzzaman in a case filed over assaulting an on-duty security official and obstructing government work at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.

The incident occurred on October 1 near the baggage belt area after passengers arriving from Madina on a Biman flight faced luggage delays and a shortage of trolleys, leading to agitation among passengers.

According to the complaint, Akhtaruzzaman allegedly hurled abuse at Airport Executive Director Group Captain SM Ragib Samad and threatened to 'grab him by the neck and throw him out.'

The situation escalated when security supervisor Warrant Officer Mohammad Kamal Uddin asked people accompanying the lawmaker to stop filming in a restricted area. Akhtaruzzaman allegedly verbally abused and physically assaulted him.

The case statement further alleges that the lawmaker threw bottles of Zamzam water off trolleys, damaging them, and behaved rudely toward a Biman representative.

Akhtaruzzaman was arrested from his residence in the Dhaka Cantonment area on October 2 and was placed on a one-day remand before being sent to jail.

The former lawmaker, who joined Jamaat-e-Islami in December last year after being expelled from the BNP, remains in custody.

headline_marked: US lab [[tests AI-designed virus in human]] to fight superbugs
headline: US lab tests AI-designed virus in human to fight superbugs
summary: California-based Radical Numerics has administered an AI-created bacteriophage to a patient with limited medical options in a first-of-its-kind experiment.
details: An artificial intelligence research lab in California has administered a custom AI-designed virus to a human patient for the first time in an attempt to combat antibiotic-resistant superbugs.
The experimental treatment, named Omnii-1, was delivered under a physician-led compassionate-use pathway for a patient with limited remaining medical options.
If verified through peer-reviewed research, this would mark the first time AI-designed bacteriophages—viruses that specifically target and destroy bacteria—have been used in humans.
Traditional phage therapy usually requires lengthy searches through environmental collections to find a match for a specific infection.
Radical Numerics claims its AI model, trained on genomic data and phage-host interactions, can rapidly generate tailored phages on demand.
The company synthesized the viral variants to verify their viability and activity before administration, though clinical outcomes remain undisclosed for patient privacy.
caption:
For the first time, an AI-designed virus has been administered to a human patient to fight superbugs.

An artificial intelligence research lab in California has administered a custom AI-designed virus to a human patient for the first time in an attempt to combat antibiotic-resistant superbugs.

The experimental treatment, named Omnii-1, was delivered under a physician-led compassionate-use pathway for a patient with limited remaining medical options.

If verified through peer-reviewed research, this would mark the first time AI-designed bacteriophages—viruses that specifically target and destroy bacteria—have been used in humans.

Traditional phage therapy usually requires lengthy searches through environmental collections to find a match for a specific infection.

Radical Numerics claims its AI model, trained on genomic data and phage-host interactions, can rapidly generate tailored phages on demand.

The company synthesized the viral variants to verify their viability and activity before administration, though clinical outcomes remain undisclosed for patient privacy.
